reuse: Original unified solve incumbent and its two already sealed training-fold predictions. The designated validation score and past research folds are known development results.
discovery: Fit every newly installed generic paired-text encoder with linear and diagonal-quadratic utilities on the official primary training partition. This research screen measures four new heads. The same lexical, style and training-corpus familiarity features are available to each. Compare each alone and a prespecified equal probability average with the frozen incumbent on the same rows.
confirmation: Lock the top two distinct deployment options by primary accuracy, breaking ties in favor of fewer members then lexical ID. Confirm those two on confirmation_1. Require positive accuracy gain over the matched incumbent on both folds and pooled gain of at least 0.003 across both. Choose the eligible option with greatest worst-fold gain, then pooled gain then fewer members. If eligible, check once on separately grouped confirmation_2 against the same incumbent configuration. A third-fold loss precludes course evaluation. If none qualify, retain the incumbent and continue with a genuinely different mechanism.
validation: Only a frozen winner may be refit on all training data and evaluated once on designated validation. Keep the historical course test and H2 sealed. Study heads forced for coverage are research measurements, not a claim that the default agent chose them. Any claimed course upgrade must also be exercised from raw inputs with autonomous selection and raw inference.
training_scope: The primary and two confirmation evaluation partitions are grouped by shared texts. Their fitting partitions overlap. Frozen, label-free features may be reused by exact input text and model revision. All word counts, scales and supervised heads refit only on the current fitting rows.
